answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before its votes or trades count, then weight influence by bonded value rather than account count. A river of fresh accounts no longer creates free power: each one needs its own capital, and provable fraud burns that bond. The cost scales with the influence sought, while honest newcomers can still join with small stakes; an orchard of identities is possible, but not costless, and ivory tokens matter only if they have real value.
